To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the use of a multilingual classifier for earthquake events is feasible and can be adapted to the language of origin; (2) the use of multilingual classifiers can help to confirm earthquake parameters; (3) the use of SMT can be used to translate tweets into English.

(a) the detection of earthquake events from twitter messages is possible by using a set of classifiers that are language-specific and (b) the translation of underresourced languages into English is a prerequisite for multilingual information extraction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the detection of earthquakes and tsunamis in Twitter messages and the extraction of information from them.
the detection of earthquake events in the endangered zones, and the extraction of relevant information for the purpose of crisis management.
the development of multilingual text mining tools that can be used in emergency situations to support the access and the translation of relevant information from social media.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the multilingual nature of social media has been recognized as a major challenge, and a variety of approaches have been proposed to deal with this challenge, but no general solution exists so far.
the current research is still at a very early stage and that more research is needed in order to support multilingual analysis in the future.
multilinguality is a major problem for the analysis of social media in the context of emergency events.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we are currently focusing on earthquake and tsunami detection in the Mediterranean area and that our long-term goal is to extend the work on earthquake detection to other events like floods, forest fires, and volcanic eruptions and to develop a system that supports the translation of relevant keywords into English.
we try to combine state of the art methods for text classification with statistical machine translation to support the detection and analysis of emergency events.
it is possible to detect earthquake events from Twitter messages in the Mediterranean and to extract keywords that can be used for further analysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that

it is possible to detect earthquake and tsunami events in the Mediterranean region by filtering out irrelevant tweets and to confirm forecast parameters for tsunami affecting coastal areas, where no tide gaugers exist and which can be integrated into seimographic sensor networks.

the translation of relevant information into a “lingua franca”, like English, can help to improve the situational awareness of emergency management teams and to reduce the time needed for decision-making.
the development of a multilingual system for emergency response requires a careful selection of languages to be supported and the development of a codebook that enables rapid translation.
